corridor: Haarlemmerweg, Amsterdam — Molenwerf (west) to Solebaystraat (east), both sides, including the corner buildings that front Haarlemmerweg from Gibraltarstraat, Van Gentstraat, Kijkduinstraat, Livornostraat, Solebaystraat and Nieuwpoortstraat
userCorridorLabel: The user typed "Haarlemmerdijk"; the screenshot corridor (Kennedy Van der Laan, WJ Digital Marketing, MB limousines and Gymbase Westerpark to the north; Stichting De Gibraltar, Amsterdam Skin care, Taco Lindo West and Dojo Doorje to the south) is this Haarlemmerweg stretch, and that is what is inventoried.

phase2.note: The three TRACK_M pands with usable corridor-facing panorama evidence, taken in this lane.

nextSteps.STREET_SURVEY: The 1930s and 1980s rows on the south side (Haarlemmerweg 485-645 and the Gibraltarstraat / Van Gentstraat / Kijkduinstraat / Livornostraat / Solebaystraat corners) are repetitive frontages: they need the block-face / block-kit street survey (one rhythm per block face, shared facade recipe), not one large recipe or bespoke model per address. Those blocks carry the shopfronts the user photographed (Stichting De Gibraltar, Amsterdam Skin care, Taco Lindo West, Dojo Doorje).
nextSteps.TRACK_L: No pand in this window is a pre-1900 ornamented historic front, so this corridor produced no TRACK_L row. If the 1930s corner blocks at Haarlemmerweg 507-519 (decorative brick fronts over shopfronts) are judged ornamented enough to need a bespoke builder rather than the block-face survey, they are the only Track L candidates here and need a Track L lane with its own inventory and elevations.
nextSteps.NO_EVIDENCE: Molenwerf 1, Molenwerf 2 and Haarlemmerweg 518A are TRACK_M-shaped but no panorama reaches a corridor-facing wall (the Molenwerf blocks sit 29-38 m back behind their forecourt, and 518A is a 2023 tower whose road wall the 2022 capture does not cover). They stay unbuilt until a panorama, a Beeldbank photo or another open source shows the front.
